By Anthony Fenech
Detroit Free Press

The Tigers were destined to take a position player with the No. 5 pick in the 2019 MLB Draft all along – high school outfielder Riley Greene ended up being the choice – but as the team made its final preparations for the draft, enough consideration was given to Texas Christian left-hander Nick Lodolo.
Detroit’s biggest organizational need of an impact offensive bat would win out in the end, but perhaps there was another factor: Class A Lakeland lefty Tarik Skubal.

A year after the Tigers chose Skubal in the ninth round of the 2018 draft, he has opened eyes as a pitcher with the potential to join top prospects Casey Mize and Matt Manning as their lefty compliments in a future starting rotation.

“In his first year after the draft, in an advanced league like Lakeland, he’s put up real good numbers,” Tigers vice president of player development Dave Littlefield said. “He’s commanding his pitches, using three pitches very effectively.”
In 11 starts with the Flying Tigers, Skubal has posted a 3.42 ERA and 1.04 WHIP. Most impressively, he’s struck out 64 batters in 55 1/3 innings, good for a strikeouts-per-nine innings ratio of 10.4.

Skubal was drafted out of Kingman Academy in Arizona, and made an immediate impression last season, dominating his way from the Gulf Coast League to Class A West Michigan in 22 1/3 innings. To control his innings, Skubal was used mainly in relief, though he is a starting pitcher by trade, and has assumed that role in 2019.
Skubal, 22, underwent elbow ligament reconstruction surgery in 2016.
“We wanted to be cautious and make sure that going into 2019, we had a healthy guy,” Littlefield said.

The scouting community is slightly in favor of Skubal sticking as a starter, with four pitches at his disposal, including a low-to-mid 90 mph fastball, though refinement is certainly necessary in climbing the ladder, especially with his breaking pitches. He throws both a curveball and slider.
Given Skubal’s strong start this season, and his pitchability, a promotion to Double-A Erie might not be far away.

“The players kind of point you in the direction with where to go and the numbers that he’s put up as a first full-season guy, they’re impressive,” Littlefield said. “Very mature, definitely advanced – he’s a smart, competitive guy who knows what he’s doing out there.

“Obviously, there’s room for improvement at this stage in their professional career, but he looks very good. That’s certainly within the scope of things if he continues at this pace, possibly going to Double-A.”
Anthony Fenech
Detroit Free Press
Tigers beat writer
